history.gap: The markets region is a ledger of nouns, not a designed moment: nine serif rows, three orphan tickers (NQ, ES, XAUUSD) with the other six rows bare, so the right column reads as unfinished rather than deliberate, and the desktop crop leaves the left third of the container empty above a 130px dead band before "06 Live". At the bar every row would carry the same secondary datum (or none), the group headers would do real typographic work (a display-size "Indices" with the count, not a 10px tracked label), and the section would have one moment of scale contrast instead of uniform 22px rows.
history.motion: Plain scroll with a sticky header and rotated margin label; no reveals, no easing visible, restrained to the point of static.
history.verdict: A is a quiet, consistent editorial ledger with a coherent hairline system (solid rows, gold dashed groups) and clean small caps, but it never rises above competent and its inconsistent tickers and dead band keep it off a shortlist. B has the atmosphere and photographic ambition of a stronger site, yet illegible copy over imagery, a logo collision, missing-space text bugs and a struck-through mobile nav are craft failures a jury cannot forgive, so the restrained one wins.

history.gap: The markets list is immaculate but inert: four rows of nouns set at one size, with the entire left third of the viewport (0–560px) empty apart from tiny right-aligned labels, and on mobile the section flips from left-aligned rows to a centred "WAT / De oprichter" block. At the bar, the list would carry one designed moment — a large numeral count, a wide-measure display line, or the ticker tags (NQ, ES, XAUUSD) promoted into a true second column on a shared baseline — and the mobile section would keep a single alignment axis, with Dow Jones not orphaned onto its own row in the two-column grid.
history.motion: Restrained staggered row fade-ins with a scroll-spy vertical section label; nothing over-eased, nothing gratuitous, though the rows simply fade rather than settle.
history.verdict: A is a disciplined editorial ledger — warm hairlines, aligned ticker tags, a cool serif/small-caps pairing — that is correct in every pixel but never rises above tasteful. B has the more cinematic ambition, yet on screen it is a hero with overlapping labels, unreadable copy over imagery, broken text animation and a strikethrough nav, so A wins comfortably on craft while neither reaches the shortlist.
